full_judgment:
10. On behalf of the contesting defendants, defendant No. 19 Jogendra Lal Chowdhury was examined. He deposed for the defendants 16 and 18. This witness however, disclaimed any interest of his own in the suit land. He stated that he was a benamder of his maternal uncle in respect of the auction purchase. He denied any knowledge about the Will or the probate. According to him R.S. and P.S. khatians are correct. This witness, however, was claiming his presence at the time of the kabalas but he did not see any agreement. 

 12. An agreement dated 22-1-1962 was marked as Ext. A(1). Exhibit B(1) to B(5) are certain kabalas. Exhibit C I series are certain mortgage deeds. Exhibit D I series are the sale certificates. Exhibit E I series is the writ of delivery of possession. Exhibit Flseries are the copy of orders relating to delivery of possession. Exhibit GI is the copy of plaint in Title suit No. 99 of 1944. Exhibit HI is the certified copy of a patta. Exhibit 41) series are R.S. and P.S. khatians whereas. Exhibit J series are certain dakhilas. Exhibit K1 is the certified copy of demand notice Exhibit LI series are certain challans and Exhibit MI is the certified copy of the order sheet in certain title suits. These are all the documents put in evidence on behalf of the contesting defendants. 

 28. Mr. Halder has drawn our attention to a decision of a Single Bench of this Court in the case Afser Molla and another V. Abdul Aziz and others reported its 29 D.L.R. 416. In that case section 20 of the Trust Act and Article 148 of the Limitation Act were considered. In the instant case these provisions are not involved. This case therefore, is of no assistance to Mr. Haider. We have indicated earlier that defendant No. 16 group has been claiming title and possession on the basis of auction purchase for a period over 12 years. It has been admitted by P.W.1 that Defdts have their homestead and some pucca structures in certain portion of the suit lands. It is also in the evidence of P.W I that Mohendra died in 1953 and he came to know about the will after the death of Mohendra. The defence contention on the other hand is that they are in possession of their purchased land from the date of such purchase. It is difficult for us to rely upon the uncorroborated testimony of the plaintiffs that he had no knowledge as to the possession of the defendant No. 16 group in the homestead and the tank. In this view of the matter Mr. Rub has drawn our attention to Article 134 of the Limitation Act for the purpose of the suit. Article 134 provides for a suit within 12 years from the date the transfer becomes known to the plaintiff in order to recover possession of immoveable property conveyed or bequeathed in trust or mortgaged and afterwards transferred by the trustee or mortgagee for a valuable consideration. We have earlier held that the transfer was made by Mohendra a trustee under Exhibit 2 to the Will in contravention of certain terms. Therefore, such a suit for recovery of possession appears to be contemplated by the said Article. It is 12 years from the date of the transfer being known to the plaintiff. The plaintiff did not say in his evidence that the transfer of the homestead and the tank in favour of defendant No 18 and 16 as claimed by them was not known to him. It rather appears from his admission that the homestead of the defendants was known to him and to his knowledge, pucca structures in certain portions were built; if that is so, it was for the plaintiff to prove that he was within 12 years from his knowledge of the transfer. We find it difficult to rely upon his evidence that he had no knowledge of the transfer of the homestead and the tank as appearing in schedule B of the plaint. This homestead and the adjoining tank, in our opinion, cannot be recovered from the possession of defendant No. 16 group. In the circumstances we hold that the interest of defendant No. 16 as it now stands in the homestead and the tank remains unaffected and the suit is not liable to succeed to that extent for recovery of possession. We have no reason to disbelieve the long possession of defendant No. 16 group in the homestead and the tank and connected khatian and dakhilas supporting such claim. In this view of the matter we modify the decree of the learned Subordinate Judge to this extent. For the reasons stated above the appeal succeeds in part, namely, in respect of the homestead and the tank appertaining to Schedule (B) of the plaint as claimed by defendants Nos. 16 and 18. Barring the extent indicated above, the decree of the trial Court needs no interference.
